newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA FUND ACCEPTS BIDS FOR LARGEST CEMENT MAKER.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA FUND ACCEPTS BIDS FOR LARGEST CEMENT MAKER.

text.p: Romania's State Ownership Fund (FPS), the country's main privatisation body, said on Wednesday it had accepted five bids for the purchase of a 50.98 percent stake in the largest local cement maker Romcim.
"We accepted all the bids we had for Romcim and negotiations with the five bidders will start on Friday," FPS president Sorin Dimitriu told a news conference.
Bids had been previously offered by Britain's building materials producer and supplier RMC Group Plc and France's Lafarge cement maker.
Also bidding were construction group Heidelberger Zement AG of Germany, Spain's Valenciana de Cementos Portland and Romanian private company Grivco SA.
Bids and the minimum price were confidential, the FPS said.

Romcim has a capital of around 387 billion lei in shares with a face value of 25,000 lei each. It was included in the mass selloff, which resulted in a shareholding structure with Romanian private shareholders having 38 percent and the State Ownership Fund holding 62 percent.
The company trades on Romania's over-the-counter market. On Tuesday it closed at 122,000 lei, 2,000 up from Monday.
